artboards.title: A · One list, the money down it (chosen)
B · By the keyword that bought them

annotations.text:
What people typed: two ways to draw it, replacing today's two cards (Search terms, Negatives). Both keep what the cards do: every search your keywords bought, with what it cost and sold; block one search from its row, or a family of them by their words, with what the block would catch shown before you make it. Try it: block a row, type other words into Block words, switch to this week only.
Real figures from the engine: seed 1, Vella & Co. at mid-price performance, after week 6, with the makeover canvas's keywords (four phrase at ₹33, two broad at ₹24, the brand on exact at ₹57): 33 searches from 7 keywords. Block words opens on "squat proof" on broad, to show a block that also catches a search that sells.

Chosen by the owner, 2026-09-15. A · One list, the money down it. Every search in one list, most spent first, with its sales, what a sale cost there and how many came back; Block words beside it, and the rows it would catch are outlined in the list as you type.
For: it is the real search terms report, redrawn; the searches that cost most sit on top, and it needs nothing the engine does not already report.
Against: why a search is there, which of your keywords reached it, is not on the screen.

B · By the keyword that bought them. The same searches under the keyword that reached each one, so a broad keyword's reach is drawn: under running leggings women sit flared leggings women and casual leggings women, marked with the word they lack. Block words beside it, the same.
For: it shows broad match wandering, the lesson of the guide's "How far broad match wanders", on your own keywords; real Google Ads shows the keyword beside each search.
Against: the engine works out which keyword bought each search every week and then drops it, so this needs one addition to what the engine reports (the keyword, nothing it computes); and a search two keywords bought over the weeks needs a rule for where it sits.

Two things drawing it found in today's cards, both from the game counting sales as expected fractions. The mark for a search that took five clicks and sold nothing never fires here, because no search that ever converts reads as zero: how to wash gym leggings cost ₹3,566 for 0.8 sales and goes unmarked. Both options mark instead a sale that costs over twice your ₹488 average, beside today's returns mark (more came back than your 26%). And the block preview's warning, "this would also block searches that converted for you", fires for almost any search you have bought, for the same reason; both options show the sales and let the amber mark say which ones matter.
